reason: Economic evaluation (cost-effectiveness analysis) alongside a randomized controlled trial, not an RCT itself; population is patients with first or second CDI episode, not recurrent CDI.
evidence: Abstract: 'FMT is currently recommended for patients with three or more CDI episodes. A recent RCT shows that FMT may be considered early, defined as intervention during the first or second CDI episode. The aim was to investigate hospital costs of FMT as a complementary treatment compared with current standard care in patients with first or second CDI.' Title: 'Cost-effectiveness of faecal microbiota transplantation compared with vancomycin monotherapy for early Clostridioides difficile infection: economic evaluation alongside a randomized controlled trial.'

reason: Trial enrollment/recruitment report for an ongoing RCT of capsule FMT for prevention of recurrent CDI in the VA system; does not report clinical outcomes (cure/resolution/recurrence), only enrollment numbers and methods.
evidence: Abstract: 'This is a randomized comparison of capsule-delivered fecal microbiota transplant for the prevention of recurrent [CDI]. A total of 102 participants have been enrolled through January 2021. Centralized case identification and in-home enrollment has facilitated enrollment from 34 unique states.' Published in Clinical Trials journal as a recruitment/methods report with no outcome data.

reason: Double-blind randomized two-arm pilot multicenter RCT of standard FMT capsules vs FMT enriched with Lactobacillus for patients with recurrent CDI, reporting CDI resolution and bowel movement reduction at 90-day follow-up.
evidence: Full text: 'We designed a double-blinded randomized comparative two-arm pilot multicenter study to compare the efficacy and impact in the intestinal microbiome of standard FMT delivered by capsules (FMT) [vs FMT-L].' Population: 'Participants were patients ≥16 years of age diagnosed with a recurrence of CDI.' Outcomes: 'CDI resolution was considered by the absence of diarrhea, leukocytosis, and abdominal pain at the end of treatment.' Results: 'Overall, both groups had a reduction in bowel movements per day, from 8.6 to 3.2 in the first 48 h (62.7% reduction).' Published 2019 in Canadian Journal of Gastroenterology & Hepatology.
